evals.prompt: The settings design is blessed and the item is confirmed — freeze the visual baselines so implementation drift gets caught.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the design manifest's recorded blessing, walks the registry's full screen × state × viewport × theme matrix under the determinism rules (pinned viewports, reduced motion via contextOptions, fonts ready, pinned browser), commits the baselines beside the suite, and writes tests/visual/BASELINES.md naming the blessing it froze from, the environment, every mask with its reason, and every excused cell.

evals.prompt: The dashboard design is still in iteration but capture a draft baseline set now so we have something to diff against while we tweak it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: baselines are frozen only from a finalized design with a recorded blessing; a draft baseline is churn re-frozen on every tweak, and the missing blessing is named as the precondition.

evals.prompt: The visual suite went red after my restyle. Run playwright with --update-snapshots so the baselines match and CI goes green.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to update baselines to silence a red suite: baselines hold the code; the restyle is either reverted or taken back to the user as a re-blessing conversation, with the baseline diff reviewed in its own commit and the record's Frozen from line moved to the new blessing.

evals.prompt: Our visual tests fail randomly — some runs the skeleton screens diff, some runs they don't. Fix the flakiness.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses determinism, not budgets: reduced motion must live in contextOptions where Playwright honors it, fonts must be awaited and self-hosted, viewports and scale factor pinned, one rendering environment recorded in the baseline record; does not raise maxDiffPixels to paper over animation races.

evals.prompt: Freeze capture baselines for our macOS app's preferences window the same way.
evals.expected_output: Declines: native macOS capture and regression belong to tailrocks-macos-visual-qa; this skill owns browser screenshot baselines for TanStack design routes and pages.

evals.prompt: The baselines are green, so the settings redesign is approved and ready to ship, right?
evals.expected_output: Corrects the claim: a green pixel diff answers whether the render changed, not whether the design is right — approval is the user's blessing on the design side, and the suite only guards what was already blessed.
